knowledge:
- key_parameters: <x=Input data, either a data matrix with positional information or a GRanges object with data stored in metadata columns ;; maxbp=Restricts the maximum sojourn time to limit model complexity ;; J=Number of states in the HSMM model, which can be explicitly defined or estimated using xAnno ;; soj.type=Type of sojourn distribution, such as 'gamma' to incorporate positional information ;; emis.type=Distribution of emission probability, such as 'norm' for continuous log-ratios, 'pois'/'nbinom' for count data, or 'mvnorm'/'mvt' for multivariate data ;; com.emis=Logical value controlling whether emission density is estimated globally across all regions (TRUE) or locally per region (FALSE) ;; prior.m=Method to determine emission parameter priors, either 'quantile' (using q.alpha and r.var) or 'cluster' (automatic clustering) ;; grp=Vector assigning data columns to experimental groups for simultaneous or iterative modeling ;; maxseg=Maximum number of segments per chromosome region for biomvRseg ;; family=Distribution family for biomvRseg, such as 'norm' or 'pois'>
- alternatives: <DNACopy (CBS algorithm)=Mentioned as a traditional method for copy number segmentation, compared with biomvRseg which uses BIC/mBIC penalties ;; tilingArray=The segmentation method in biomvRseg is an extension of the tilingArray algorithm, adapted to handle Poisson and Negative Binomial distributions ;; BiSeq=Mentioned for DMR detection; biomvRCNS offers an alternative by using HSMM to model both methylation differences and p-values simultaneously using multivariate normal emissions>
- when_to_use: <Use this package when you have multivariate genomic profiles across multiple samples, conditions, or replicates (e.g., tiling arrays, RNA-seq, aCGH, or bisulfite sequencing) and need to segment the genome into functional states like copy number states, transcripts, or differentially methylated regions.>
- pitfalls: <The package does not perform data normalization or correction; input data must be pre-normalized and corrected for batch effects or factors of interest before analysis ;; Input data must be sorted by genomic position before being passed to the models ;; For non-continuous regions on the same chromosome, users must assign different seqnames to each part, as biomvRhsmm sequentially processes each unique seqname as a single continuous chromosome>

workflows.name: acgh_copy_number_segmentation
workflows.intent: Segment array CGH (aCGH) data to identify genomic regions of copy number deletion, duplication, or neutrality across multiple samples.
input: coriell.txt (aCGH log2 ratio data frame containing clone names, chromosome, genomic position, and sample columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load data and construct a sorted GRanges object ;; 2. Run the Hidden Semi-Markov Model (HSMM) segmentation using biomvRhsmm ;; 3. Visualize the segmentation results using biomvRGviz ;; 4. Run alternative homogeneous segmentation using biomvRseg ;; 5. Run alternative max-gap-min-run segmentation using biomvRmgmr
workflows.code:
data('coriell', package='biomvRCNS')
head(coriell, n=3)
xgr<-GRanges(seqnames=coriell[,2], 
	IRanges(start=coriell[,3], width=1, names=coriell[,1]))
values(xgr)<-DataFrame(coriell[,4:5], row.names=NULL)
xgr<-sort(xgr)
head(xgr, n=3)
rhsmm<-biomvRhsmm(x=xgr, maxbp=1E5, J=3, soj.type='gamma', 
	com.emis=T, emis.type='norm', prior.m='quantile', grp=c(1,2))
show(rhsmm)
obj<-biomvRGviz(exprgr=xgr[seqnames(xgr)=='11', 'Coriell.05296'], 
	seggr=rhsmm@res[mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'SAMPLE']=='Coriell.05296'], tofile=FALSE)
rseg<-biomvRseg(x=xgr, maxbp=4E4, maxseg=10, family='norm', grp=c(1,2))
head(rseg@res)
rmgmrh<-biomvRmgmr(xgr, q=0.9, high=T, maxgap=1000, minrun=2500, grp=c(1,2))
rmgmrl<-biomvRmgmr(xgr, q=0.1, high=F, maxgap=1000, minrun=2500, grp=c(1,2))
res<-c(rmgmrh@res, rmgmrl@res)

workflows.name: rna_seq_transcript_detection
workflows.intent: Detect expressed transcripts (exons, introns, and intergenic regions) from RNA-seq read count data using gene annotations as priors.
input: encodeTP53.RData (pre-compiled GRanges object containing window-based read counts and regional gene annotations)
TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene (UCSC hg19 known gene database for sojourn and state priors)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and pool replicate read counts for different cell types ;; 2. Run biomvRhsmm with a TxDb annotation object to automatically estimate state number and sojourn parameters ;; 3. Extract detected exon segments ;; 4. Plot the expression and estimated segments against gene annotations using biomvRGviz ;; 5. Identify novel transcribed regions by overlapping results with annotations
workflows.code:
data(encodeTP53)
cgr<-encodeTP53$cgr
gmgr<-encodeTP53$gmgr
mcols(cgr)<-DataFrame(
	Gm12878=1+rowSums(as.matrix(mcols(cgr)[,1:2])), 
	K562=1+rowSums(as.matrix(mcols(cgr)[,3:4])) )
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene)
txdb<-TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene	
rhsmm<-biomvRhsmm(x=cgr, xAnno=txdb, maxbp=1E3, soj.type='gamma', 
	emis.type='pois', prior.m='quantile', q.alpha=0.01)
rhsmm@res[mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'STATE']=='exon']
g<-mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'STATE']=='exon' & mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'SAMPLE']=='Gm12878'
obj<-biomvRGviz(exprgr=cgr[,'Gm12878'], gmgr=gmgr, 
	seggr=rhsmm@res[g], plotstrand='-', regionID='TP53', tofile=FALSE)
k<-mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'STATE']=='exon' & mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'SAMPLE']=='K562'
obj<-biomvRGviz(exprgr=cgr[,'K562'], gmgr=gmgr, 
  seggr=rhsmm@res[k], plotstrand='-', regionID='TP53', tofile=FALSE)
nK2gm<-queryHits(findOverlaps(rhsmm@res[k], gmgr))
nK2G<-queryHits(findOverlaps(rhsmm@res[k], rhsmm@res[g]))
rhsmm@res[k][setdiff(seq_len(sum(k)), unique(c(nK2G, nK2gm)))]
rseg<-biomvRseg(x=cgr, maxbp=1E3, maxseg=20, family='pois')
rmgmr<-biomvRmgmr(x=cgr, q=0.99, maxgap=50, minrun=100)

workflows.name: dmr_detection
workflows.intent: Identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) by combining methylation differences and statistical significance levels.
input: variosm.RData (GRanges object containing methylation differences and p-values for CpG sites)
workflows.stages: 1. Load methylation data ;; 2. Run univariate biomvRhsmm on both profiles using cluster-based emission priors ;; 3. Intersect high methylation difference segments with low p-value segments to define DMRs ;; 4. Alternatively, run multivariate biomvRhsmm using a multivariate Normal emission distribution to model covariance ;; 5. Extract high-confidence DMRs and plot results
workflows.code:
data(variosm)
head(variosm, n=3)
rhsmm<-biomvRhsmm(x=variosm, maxbp=100, prior.m='cluster', maxgap=100)
hiDiffgr<-rhsmm@res[mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'STATE']!=2 
	& mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'SAMPLE']=='meth.diff']
dirNo<-mcols(hiDiffgr)[,'STATE']=='1' & mcols(hiDiffgr)[,'AVG']>0 |
	mcols(hiDiffgr)[,'STATE']=='3' & mcols(hiDiffgr)[,'AVG']<0	
hiDiffgr<- hiDiffgr[!dirNo]
loPgr<-rhsmm@res[mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'STATE']==1
	& mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'SAMPLE']=='p.val']
DMRs<-reduce(intersect(hiDiffgr, loPgr), min.gapwidth=100)
idx<-findOverlaps(variosm, DMRs, type='within')
mcols(DMRs)<-DataFrame(cbind(TYPE='DMR', aggregate(as.data.frame(mcols(variosm[queryHits(idx)])), 
	by=list(DMR=subjectHits(idx)), FUN=median)[,-1]))
names(DMRs)<-paste0('DMRs', seq_along(DMRs))	
DMRs
plot(rhsmm, gmgr=DMRs, tofile=FALSE)
rhsmm<-biomvRhsmm(x=variosm, J=6, maxbp=100, emis.type='mvnorm',
 prior.m='cluster', maxgap=100, com.emis=T)
plot(rhsmm, tofile=FALSE)
DMRs<-reduce(rhsmm@res[mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'STATE']=='6'], min.gapwidth=100)
idx<-findOverlaps(variosm, DMRs, type='within')
mcols(DMRs)<-DataFrame(cbind(TYPE='DMR', aggregate(as.data.frame(mcols(variosm[queryHits(idx)])), 
	by=list(DMR=subjectHits(idx)), FUN=median)[,-1], stringsAsFactors=F))
names(DMRs)<-paste0('DMRs', seq_along(DMRs))
DMRs
cDMRs<-reduce(rhsmm@res[mcols(rhsmm@res)[,'STATE']=='5'], min.gapwidth=100)
idx<-findOverlaps(variosm, cDMRs, type='within')
mcols(cDMRs)<-DataFrame(cbind(TYPE='cDMR', aggregate(as.data.frame(mcols(variosm[queryHits(idx)])), 
	by=list(cDMRs=subjectHits(idx)), FUN=median)[,-1], stringsAsFactors=F))
names(cDMRs)<-paste0('cDMRs', seq_along(cDMRs))
cDMRs
rhsmm@param$emis.par['chr1',][[1]]
rhsmm@param$soj.par['chr1',][[1]]
plot(rhsmm, gmgr=c(DMRs, cDMRs), tofile=FALSE)
